 2   Q.      Please state your name and address.

 3   A.      My name is Will McAdams. My business address is 1122 Colorado Street, Suite 2323,

 4           Austin, Texas 78701.

 5   Q.      By whom are you employed and in what capacity?

 6   A.      I am the President of McAdams Energy Group, LLC.

 7   Q.      On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

 8   A.      I am filing testimony on behalf of the M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners: 27

 9           landowners in Menard and Mason Counties who own over 10,000 acres of the 15,639 acres
10           that would be directly impacted by Links M31, M32, and M33. 1
11   Q.      Are you the same Will McAdams who filed direct testimony on behalf of the M31,

12           M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners in this proceeding?

13   A.      Yes.

14   Q.      Are you sponsoring any attachments with your cross-rebuttal testimony?

15   A.      No.

16   Q.      Was your cross-rebuttal testimony prepared by you or under your direct supervision

17           and control?

18   A.      Yes.

19   Q.      Is the information contained in your cross-rebuttal testimony true and correct to the

20           best of your knowledge and belief?

21   A.      Yes.

                See M31, M32, and M33 Opposition Landowners' First Supplemental First Amended Motion to Intervene
     (Apr. 27, 2026) (listing 25 landowners with a combined 9,645 acres that would be directly impacted by Links M31,

     (adding two landowners with a combined 416 acres that would be directly impacted by Links M31, M32, and M33).


     Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Will McAdams                                                                 4 of 19
  1                                    II.       S UMMARY OF T ESTIMONY

 2   Q.     What is the scope of your cross-rebuttal testimony in this proceeding?

 3   A.     First, I compare Route 894 of the Bell County East Switch – Big Hill Substation 765-

 4          kilovolt (“kV”) transmission line project (“Proposed Transmission Line Project”) to Routes

 5          572 and CCG, which were recommended by certain intervenors.

 6                    Second, I express my concerns that Routes 572 and CCG increase reliability and

 7          resiliency risks by crossing and paralleling the San Saba River and Colorado River for a

 8          longer distance than Route 894.

 9                    Third, I describe how Route CCG creates a single point of failure for multiple trans-

10          mission lines at the San Saba River crossing.

11                    And fourth, I explain that Route CCG does not appear to be forward-progressing

12          route based on its roundabout path from the intersection of Links J33, J6, and K41 to the

13          intersection of Links L2, L4, and M22.

14                    For those reasons, I recommend that the Public Utility Commission of Texas

15          (“Commission”) not approve Routes 572 or CCG.

16   Q.     Do you rebut certain recommendations and arguments advanced by the other inter-

17          venors’ witnesses?

18   A.     Yes. My testimony rebuts the routing recommendations proposed by two environmental-

19          consultant witnesses for a handful of intervenors:

20          •     Ms. Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke on behalf of the “‘Segment K13/K51 Landowners;’

21                Cherokee Creek Partners; and Bonnie Helene McAnelly, individually and as Trustee of

22                the 2025 Homestead Trust and the Bonnie Helene McAnelly 2023 Trust”; 2 and

23          •     Mr. Aaron Brewer on behalf of “Save the Lampasas, Carpenter Land & Cattle, Martin,

24                [a]nd The N3 Opposition Landowner Group.” 3


            2
                Direct Testimony of Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke at 5:23–24 (May 13, 2026) (Reinecke Direct).
            3
                Direct Testimony of Aaron Brewer at 3:7–10 (May 13, 2026) (Brewer Direct).


     Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Will McAdams                                                                  5 of 19
  1                  III.       C OMPARISON OF R OUTE 894 TO R OUTES 572 AND CCG

 2   Q.      Did Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC and LCRA Transmission Services Cor-

 3           poration (together, “Utilities”) identify a route that best meets the statutory and reg-

 4           ulatory routing factors?

 5   A.      Yes. As I stated in my direct testimony, “out of the 122 Filed Routes, the Utilities deter-

 6           mined that Route 894 best meets the statutory and regulatory routing factors.” 4

 7   Q.      Did Mr. Brewer or Ms. Reinecke recommend alternative routes for the Proposed

 8           Transmission Line Project instead of Route 894?
 9   A.      Yes. Mr. Brewer recommends Route 572, which is one of the Utilities’ 122 Filed Routes.5
10           And Ms. Reinecke recommends a route that she calls “Cherokee Creek G” or “Route

11           CCG.” Route CCG was not one of the Utilities’ 122 Filed Routes. Instead, Route CCG was

12           created by Cherokee Creek Partners at the end of April 2026. 6

13   Q.      You previously testified that the Utilities identified the top six routes before identify-

14           ing Route 894 as the “best meets” route. Were Routes 572 and CCG in the Utilities’

15           top six routes?

16   A.      No. The Utilities identified Routes 469, 488, 495, 509, 894, and 902 as the top six routes.

17           As I previously mentioned, the Utilities narrowed the field to the “Top 6” “strongest-per-

18           forming” or “better-performing” routes “through consideration of cost, length, environ-

19           mental and land use data, engineering constraints, and public feedback received.” 7 Neither

20           Route 572 nor Route CCG was in the top six routes. And Route CCG was not included in

21           the Utilities’ 122 Filed Routes.



             4
               Direct Testimony of Will McAdams at 13:4–5 (May 13, 2026) (McAdams Direct) (citing Direct Testimony
     of Casey D. Petty, P.E. at 10:21–11:1 (Mar. 26, 2026) (Petty Direct)).

                 Brewer Direct at 25:18.

              See Cherokee Creek Partners’ Third Request for Information to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC
     and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation at 8 (Apr. 27, 2026).

 3   Q.     Do you have any concerns with Route 572 or Route CCG?

 4   A.     Yes. Routes 572 and CCG both (1) perform worse than Route 894 on the statutory and

 5          regulatory routing factors and (2) increase reliability and resiliency risks by paralleling the

 6          San Saba River and Colorado River for a longer distance than Route 894.

 7                    Additionally, Route CCG creates a potential single point of failure during a flash

 8          flood by locating the Proposed Transmission Line Project right next to an existing trans-

 9          mission line when crossing the San Saba River. And Route CCG also does not appear to be

10          a forward-progressing route.

11   A.     Routes 572 and CCG perform worse than Route 894 on the statutory and regulatory

12                                                  routing factors.

13   Q.     Have you compared the routes in this proceeding using the Utilities’ routing data?

14   A.     Yes. In my direct testimony, I compared the part of Route 894 (Links K52 and M11–M12)

15          that crosses an east-to-west distance that’s roughly analogous to Links M31–M33 (i.e.,

16          starting a few miles east of U.S. Highway 87 and ending at the intersection with north-to-

17          south Link M4 or Link M6). 8

 2            the data differentiated the routes. In other words, I excluded categories where all three

 3            routes had the same impact (e.g., number of parks or recreational areas within 1,000 feet

 4            of the route centerline or number of commercial AM radio transmitters located within

 5            10,000 feet of the route centerline).

 6   Q.       What did your comparison of Routes 894, 572, and CCG indicate?

 7   A.       Importantly, Route 894 costs $8.3 million less than Route 572 and $73.7 million less than

 8            Route CCG. Route 894 is 2.5 miles shorter than Route 572 and 9 miles shorter than Route

 9            CCG. And Route 894 impacts 22 fewer habitable structures than Route 572 and 20 fewer

10            habitable structures than Route CCG.
11                     Route 894 also (1) crosses less wetlands, streams, and lakes or ponds; 9 (2) threatens
12            less areas of high archeological/historical site potential, rare or unique plants, and recorded

13            cultural resources; and (3) impairs less combined private airstrips and FAA-registered air-

14            ports than either Route 572 or Route CCG. Route 894 parallels more existing compatible

15            rights-of-way than Route 572 but less than Route CCG (Route 894 impacts 1.35 more miles

16            of incompatible rights-of-way 10 than Route CCG does).

1   Q.     Does Route 572 perform better than Route 894 and Route CCG in any categories?
2   A.     Yes. Route 572:

3          •   crosses less cropland/hay meadow (12.77 miles) than Route CCG (13.62 miles) or

4              Route 894 (13.64 miles);

5          •   crosses less riparian areas (39.92 miles) than Route CCG (41.58 miles) or Route 894

7          •   crosses less habitat of federally listed endangered or threatened species (0.012 miles)

    Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Will McAdams                                                  10 of 19
  1          •      has a shorter estimated length of right-of-way within foreground visual zone of U.S.

 2                and State Highways (13.83 miles) than Route CCG (19.44 miles) or Route 894 (18.52

 3                miles).

 4   Q.     Does Route CCG perform better than Route 894 and Route 572 in any categories?

5    A.     Yes. Route CCG:

6           •     parallels a higher percentage of existing compatible rights-of-way (46.7%) than Route

 7                894 (43.9%) or Route 572 (40.2%); and

 8          •     crosses less agricultural cropland with mobile irrigation systems (0.11475 miles) than

 9                Route 572 (0.11477 miles) or Route 894 (0.15852 miles).

10   Q.     After comparing Routes 894, 572, and CCG, which route do you recommend?

11   A.     Among Routes 894, 572, and CCG, Route 894 best reflects and balances the statutory and

12          regulatory routing factors. Route 894 is the cheapest, shortest, and impacts the least habit-

13          able structures of those three routes.

14                    Mr. Brewer attempts to downplay Route 894’s avoidance of 22 more habitable

15          structures than Route 572 by describing Route 894’s performance as only “marginally bet-
16          ter” than Route 572. 14 But impacting over 20% less habitable structures cannot fairly be
17          described as only “marginally better”—especially when Mr. Brewer emphasizes criteria

18          like “impact to cropland or hay meadows” 15 or “impact to critical habitat for endangered

19          species” 16 where Route 572 impacts only 0.87 miles less cropland or hay meadows and

20          0.075 miles less endangered-species habitat than Route 894.

21                     Route 894 performs better than Routes 572 and CCG in six of the ten land-use and

22          environmental categories in Table WM-R2 and in all the cultural-resources categories in

23          Table WM-R2. Route 894 impacts the least private airstrips, FAA-registered airports, and

24          electronic installations (tied with Route 572).

            14
                 Brewer Direct at 24:14–15.
            15
                 Brewer Direct at 24:15–16.
            16
                 Brewer Direct at 24:18–19.


     Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Will McAdams                                                    11 of 19
  1                    Route 894 also parallels less incompatible rights-of-way than Route 572 and only

 2           1.35 more miles of incompatible rights-of-way than Route CCG. And impacting slightly

 3           less incompatible rights-of-way is insufficient to justify Route CCG’s $74 million cost pre-

 4           mium.

 5                    Again, taken together, the routing factors support Route 894 as the best route among

 6           Routes 894, 572, and CCG.

 7   B.       Routes 572 and CCG increase reliability and resiliency risks by crossing and paral-

 8            leling the San Saba River and Colorado River for a longer distance than Route 894.

 9   Q.      In your direct testimony, did you address potential reliability and resiliency risks as-

10           sociated with the Proposed Transmission Line Project?

11   A.      Yes. As I noted, the Commission must consider grid reliability and security when deter-
12           mining a route, 17 which includes considering the likelihood of any known risks in a given
13           area. I then addressed the reliability and resiliency risks associated with routing the Pro-

14           posed Transmission Line Project along and across the San Saba River, which can be the

15           site of unpredictable and devasting flash flooding.

16                    As I explained, the Proposed Transmission Line Project should cross the flood-

17           prone river at a single, perpendicular point and move immediately to higher ground and

18           more stable terrain. And if an alternative route that includes Link M31, Link M32, or Link

19           M33 is adopted, that decision would expose the grid to undue risk by placing an essential

20           segment of critical infrastructure in the path of historically known patterns of extreme flash

21           flooding. In my direct testimony, I estimated that alternative routes that include Links

22           M31–M33 would place around seven miles of the line within one mile of the San Saba

23           River, while Route 894 would place less than three miles of the line within that same dis-

24           tance.



              17
                 See 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B) (requiring the Commission to consider “grid reliability and
     security” when routing a new transmission line) (TAC).


     Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Will McAdams                                                                12 of 19
  1   Q.     Where does Route 894 cross the San Saba River?

 2   A.     Route 894 crosses the San Saba River once in San Saba County on Link K51.

 3   Q.     Do Routes 572 and CCG cross the San Saba River?

 4   A.     Yes. Route 572 includes Links M31–M33 and crosses the San Saba River once in Menard

 5          County on Link M33. Route CCG includes Link M31 and crosses the San Saba River once

 6          in McCulloch County on Link L4.

 7   Q.     Do Routes 894, 572, and CCG cross any other major rivers?

 8   A.     Yes. All three of those routes cross the Colorado River once near the Burnet County–San

 9          Saba County line. Route 894 crosses the Colorado River on Link J22, while Routes 572

10          and CCG cross on Link J31.

11   Q.     Do Routes 894, 572, and CCG cross the Lampasas River?

12   A.     No.

13   Q.     Have you reviewed the distance that Routes 894, 572, and CCG parallel the San Saba

14          River and Colorado River?

15   A.     Yes, I reviewed the Utilities maps and shapefiles to measure the length of each route that

16          crosses or parallels the Colorado River or San Saba River within less than one mile. Table

17          WM-R3 below provides the results.

               TABLE WM-R3: LENGTH OF ROUTES CROSSING OR PARALLELING MAJOR RIVERS
                            River:              Route 894:         Route 572:           Route CCG:
                   Colorado River                2.43 miles         4.42 miles             4.42 miles
                   San Saba River                2.71 miles         7.17 miles             4.47 miles
                            Total:               5.14 miles        11.59 miles             8.89 miles

18   Q.     Based on your review of the length of each route that crosses or parallels major rivers,

19          what is your recommendation?

20   A.     I recommend Route 894 over Route 572 or Route CCG. Route 894 impacts much less of

21          the Colorado River and San Saba River (combined, 5.14 miles) than either Route 572

22          (11.59 miles) or Route CCG (8.89 miles). Again, the Commission should mitigate system-



     Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Will McAdams                                                 13 of 19
  1           reliability risks and promote system resiliency by locating the line in more stable locations

 2           that minimize the distance that the line crosses or parallels the San Saba River and Colorado

 3           River. 18

 4                     Further, as Ms. Reinecke testified, the San Saba River is designated as an ecologi-

 5           cally significant stream segment and an impaired water under Section 303(d) of the Clean

 6           Water Act. 19 And the San Saba River contains critical habitat for the Balcones spike, Texas

 7           fatmucket, Texas fawnsfoot, and Texas pimpleback mussels. 20 So the Commission should

 8           adopt a route that crosses and parallels the San Saba River to the minimum extent possible
 9           to avoid adversely affecting the sensitive ecological habitats. 21 By crossing or parallelling
10           the San Saba River for only 2.7 miles, Route 894 performs far better than Route 572 (7.2

11           miles) or Route CCG (4.5 miles) on this point.

12     C.         Route CCG creates a single point of failure for multiple transmission lines at the

13                                                  San Saba River crossing.

15           line?

16   A.      Yes. As Ms. Reinecke explained, Route CCG crosses the San Saba River on Link L4, which

17           parallels “an existing transmission line at the San Saba River.” 22 That existing transmission

18           line is AEP Texas’s Mason-to-North Brady 69-kV transmission line, 23 which was recently

19           rebuilt to 138-kV standards. 24 According to the Utilities’ maps, Route CCG would locate

 3   Q.      Do you have any concerns with locating two critical transmission lines at the same

 4           San Saba River crossing?

 5   A.      Yes. As I testified, the Proposed Transmission Line Project will be a backbone segment

 6           critical to reliability of the entire power transmission and delivery network. 25 And the ex-

 7           isting Mason-to-North Brady transmission line is critical for reliability in the City of Brady

 8           area. 26

 9                      Locating the Proposed Transmission Line Project next to the existing line at the San
